arxiv-2112-03451.title: Deep Level Set for Box-supervised Instance Segmentation in Aerial Images
arxiv-2112-03451.creator: Wentong Li, Yijie Chen, Wenyu Liu, Jianke Zhu
arxiv-2112-03451.description: Abstract Box-supervised instance segmentation has recently attracted lots of research efforts while little attention is received in aerial image domain. In contrast to the general object collections, aerial objects have large intra-class variances and inter-class similarity with complex background. Moreover, there are many tiny objects in the high-resolution satellite images.

arxiv-2208-00445.title: Propagation properties in a multi-species SIR reaction-diffusion system.
arxiv-2208-00445.creator: Romain Ducasse, Samuel Nordmann
arxiv-2208-00445.description: Abstract We consider a multi-species reaction-diffusion system that arises in epidemiology to describe the spread of several strains, or variants, of a disease in a population. Our model is a natural spatial, multi-species, extension of the classical SIR model of Kermack and McKendrick.

arxiv-2303-09699.title: Fully conservative f ⁡ ( R , T ) f(R,T) gravity and Solar System constraints
arxiv-2303-09699.creator: Nicolas R. Bertini, Hermano Velten
arxiv-2303-09699.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Nicolas R. Bertini, Hermano Velten. The f ⁡ ( R , T ) f(R,T) gravity is a model whose action contains an arbitrary function of the Ricci scalar R R and the trace of the energy-momentum tensor T T .

arxiv-2305-17809.title: Ekaterina Kompantseva,
arxiv-2305-17809.description: Abstract Abstract. For an Abelian group G , any homomorphism \mu\colon G\otimes G\rightarrow G is called a multiplication on G . The set \text{Mult}\,G of all multiplications on an Abelian group G is an Abelian group with respect to addition. An Abelian group G with multiplication, defined on it, is called a ring on the group G .

arxiv-2410-04875.title: From on-shell amplitude in AdS to cosmological correlators: gluons and gravitons
arxiv-2410-04875.creator: Jiajie Mei, Yuyu Mo
arxiv-2410-04875.description: Abstract We recently introduced a recursive bootstrap method for constructing n n -point gluon and graviton Mellin-momentum amplitudes in (A)dS spacetime. The power of this approach was illustrated by our successful computation of the first five-point graviton amplitude in (A)dS.

arxiv-2501-05116.title: Conditioning of the solar corona due to large flares
arxiv-2501-05116.creator: J.K. Thalmann, M. Gupta, A.M. Veronig, Y. Liu
arxiv-2501-05116.description: Abstract Aims. We aim to better characterize the conditions of the solar corona, especially with respect to the occurrence of confined and eruptive flares. In this work, we model the coronal evolution around 231 large flares observed during solar cycle 24. Methods.

arxiv-2501-17245.title: Some limit theorems for locally stationary Hawkes processes
arxiv-2501-17245.creator: Thomas Deschatre 1 , Pierre Gruet 1 , Antoine Lotz 1,2,†
arxiv-2501-17245.description: Abstract . We prove a law of large numbers and functional central limit theorem for a class of multivariate Hawkes processes with time-dependent reproduction rate. We address the difficulties induced by the use of non-convolutive Volterra processes by recombining classical martingale methods introduced in Bacry et al. [ 3 ] with novel ideas proposed by Kwan et al.

arxiv-2504-09412.title: Deep Mismatch Channel Estimation in IRS based 6G Communication Thanks: Swapnil Saha and Md. Forkan Uddin are with the Department of Electrical and Electronic Engineering, Bangladesh University of Engineering and Technology.
arxiv-2504-09412.creator: Swapnil Saha, Md. Forkan Uddin
arxiv-2504-09412.description: Abstract We propose a channel estimation protocol to determine the uplink channel state information (CSI) at the base station for an intelligent reflecting surface (IRS) based wireless communication. More specifically, we develop a channel estimation scheme in a multi-user system with high estimation accuracy and low computational complexity.

arxiv-2505-10947.title: Certifying Stability of Reinforcement Learning Policies using Generalized Lyapunov Functions
arxiv-2505-10947.creator: Kehan Long, Jorge Cortés, Nikolay Atanasov
arxiv-2505-10947.description: Abstract Establishing stability certificates for closed-loop systems under reinforcement learning (RL) policies is essential to move beyond empirical performance and offer guarantees of system behavior. Classical Lyapunov methods require a strict stepwise decrease in the Lyapunov function but such certificates are difficult to construct for learned policies.

arxiv-2511-07478.title: Two Categorifications of the Local Langlands Correspondence for Tori
arxiv-2511-07478.creator: Ruide Fu
arxiv-2511-07478.description: Abstract . The stack of local Langlands parameters for a torus is a Picard stack. In this article, we explicitly determine its Picard dual and show that the Fourier–Mukai transform gives rise to the integral categorical local Langlands correspondence for the torus. This is the categorification of the local Langlands correspondence and answers a conjecture of X. Zhu.

arxiv-2512-13313.title: KlingAvatar 2.0 Technical Report
arxiv-2512-13313.creator: Kling Team, Kuaishou Technology
arxiv-2512-13313.description: Abstract Avatar video generation models have achieved remarkable progress in recent years. However, prior work exhibits limited efficiency in generating long duration high-resolution videos, suffering from temporal drifting, quality degradation, and a weak prompt follow-up as the video length increases. To address these challenges, we propose KlingAvatar 2.

pmc-11546858.title: The Glutamine Synthetases Are Required for Sensory Hair Cell Formation and Auditory Function in Zebrafish
pmc-11546858.creator: Yuanrong Zhao, Ziyang Wang, Mengting Xu, Fuping Qian, Guanyun Wei, Dong Liu, Pierre-Olivier Angrand
pmc-11546858.description: The development of sensory hair cells (HCs) is closely linked to hearing loss. There are still many unidentified genes that may play a crucial role in HC development and function. Glutamine synthetase, Glul, is expressed in sensory hair cells and auditory organs. However, the role of the Glul gene family in the auditory system remains largely unexplored.

pmc-11790675.title: Time-lapse imaging of identified granule cells in the mouse dentate gyrus after entorhinal lesion in vitro reveals heterogeneous cellular responses to denervation
pmc-11790675.creator: Davide Greco, Alexander Drakew, Nina Rößler, Tassilo Jungenitz, Peter Jedlicka, Thomas Deller
pmc-11790675.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Denervation of neurons is a network consequence of brain injury. The effects of denervation on neurons can be readily studied in vitro using organotypic slice cultures of entorhinal cortex and hippocampus. Following transection of the entorhino-dentate projection, granule cells (GCs) are denervated and show on average a transient loss of spines on their denervated distal dendrites but not on their non-denervated proximal dendrites.

pmc-13689210.title: Isolation of rhizobia from Ontario soils that are effective at fixing nitrogen with common bean (Phaseolus vulgaris)
pmc-13689210.creator: Tia L. Harrison, Upkardeep S. Pandher, Avery Dixon, Oona Esme, Erika M. H. Gagnon, Natalia Naranjo-Robayo, Rebecca T. Doyle, Ivan J. Oresnik, George C. diCenzo
pmc-13689210.description: Common bean (Phaseolus vulgaris) is an important crop in Canada and globally. Like other legumes, common bean establishes symbiotic interactions with nitrogen-fixing bacteria called rhizobia. However, nitrogen fixation by rhizobia in association with common bean is often suboptimal, constraining its productivity and necessitating the application of nitrogen fertilizer.

uslaw-usc-t46-s55101.title: 46 U.S.C. § 55101 — Application of coastwise laws
uslaw-usc-t46-s55101.creator: United States Congress
uslaw-usc-t46-s55101.description: United States Code, Title 46 (Shipping); Part D (Promotional Programs); Chapter 551 (Coastwise Trade). Current through Public Law 119-134, as published by the Office of the Law Revision Counsel. (a) In General.— Except as provided in subsection (b), the coastwise laws apply to the United States, including the island territories and possessions of the United States. (b) Exceptions.— The coastwise laws do not apply to— (1) American Samoa; (2) the Northern Mariana.
